articles.title: Qualcomm Validates HBC Stacked Memory Ahead of 2027 Dragonfly AI250 Sampling
articles.summary: Qualcomm today is announcing that they have completed initial validation on their High Bandwidth Compute technology. The DRAM-stacked-upon-compute architecture moves on to commercialization, with Dragonfly AI250 set to sample in the first half of 2027 The post Qualcomm Validates HBC Stacked Memory Ahead of 2027 Dragonfly AI250 Sampling appeared first on ServeTheHome .
bodyEvidence: Qualcomm this morning is announcing that it has completed the initial validation of its High Bandwidth Compute (HBC) memory architecture, which will be a central part of the company’s upcoming Dragonfly data center AI accelerators. The stacked memory architecture will see Qualcomm and its manufacturing partners place multiple layers of DRAM on top of a small compute die in order to bring memory even closer to the compute hardware that is accessing it, allowing Qualcomm to reap the energy efficiency and cost efficiency benefits of a closer hardware placement.

The recent validation of the technology moves HBC one step closer to deployment in commercial products, which are scheduled to start sampling next year. Qualcomm has now validated that the technology works and is delivering energy efficiency and memory bandwidth close to their expectations, allowing them to move towards mass production next year while keeping customers (and investors) in the loop on the development of Qualcomm’s Dragonfly AI250 accelerator and its successors.

First announced by Qualcomm back at their 2026 Investor Day , HBC is a new Qualcomm-spearheaded technology that is intending to use near-memory compute in order to strike a new balance between memory capacity, memory performance, and production costs – with Qualcomm looking to push the envelope on all three aspects.

Fundamentally, the technology is a further variation on HBM and other memory stacking technologies. But unlike HBM where multiple DRAM dies are stacked on top of a base die that is connected back to the host processor over an ultra-wide memory bus, HBC aims to cut out the middleman by placing a small compute die at the bottom of the stack instead.

In principle, placing memory on top of a compute die has several benefits. The biggest of these is energy efficiency, as moving data around costs energy – and moving large amounts of data large distances costs even more energy. By placing memory on top of a compute die, this eliminates even the relatively short distance of an HBM connection (to say nothing of external memory like LPDDR5X), minimizing the amount of energy spent to move that data around. Those energy savings, in turn, can be funneled back into improving performance of the chip itself, or allowing a larger number of chips to be clustered together within the same energy footprint.

The compute die itself is not a full processor. But by placing the most memory bandwidth-intensive operations on the die and then sending the results from that back to the larger compute die at the center of the processor, Qualcomm is looking to get their memory and compute hardware as close together as is feasible.

Qualcomm’s efforts are also eyeing production costs here. Because of the wide memory bus used by HBM, it requires advanced packaging such as CoWoS or EMIB to connect HBM stacks to a compute die and memory controllers. But by shifting most of the computational workload to the compute die that sits under the memory, far less bandwidth is needed to connect the compute die to a larger processor die elsewhere on the chip package. And, consequently, that connection can be built with cheaper technologies such as traditional 2D organic substrates.

That said, HBC does not eliminate all of the complexity. Like HBM, it still requires bonding multiple DRAM dies (or in Qualcomm’s case: wafers) on top of another die using TSVs, which is itself a challenging process. Which means the need for complex manufacturing techniques has not gone away, but it has been reduced from both memory stacking and high speed chiplet connectivity to just the memory stacking.

Finally, Qualcomm is looking to strike a better balance between memory bandwidth and memory capacity here. Notably, the company’s HBC design calls for using LPDDR5X DRAM dies rather than the thin, high-performance dies used by HBM. The company has not outlined what the final performance of the technology will be, but the capacity of an HBC stack is already projected to be larger than what current HBM4 implementations can achieve.

Qualcomm’s fundamental argument through all of this is that HBC provides a better all-around solution than any other memory architecture, be it HBM, on-die SRAM, or off-package LPDDR. As proposed, HBC has strengths and weaknesses versus all of these technologies, but as Qualcomm argues, they can achieve memory bandwidth (and thus performance) far better than external LPDDR – and approaching HBM – without the capacity constraints of using on-die SRAM, or the high costs of the latter of those two solutions.

Ultimately, all of this is meant to lead to allowing Qualcomm to build a better chip for AI inference by meeting inference’s need for memory bandwidth and capacity with fewer drawbacks than existing technologies.
Diving into the validation process itself, for their initial HBC validation Qualcomm has hooked up an early HBC sample stack to a test unit in their San Diego labs.
While the test setup itself is not much to look at, inside of it is a chip that, for Qualcomm, is critical to their data center plans.

Given that this was an early sample, it should be noted that HBC stack they were working with here just had 2 layers of DRAM dies. Shipping products will have 4 layers. So Qualcomm is not yet at the point where they are testing full-sized stacks.

Briefly outlining their validation approach, Qualcomm tells us that they used the HBC test stack with an automated tester, which was used to measure the stack as both an LPDDR5X device and as an HBC device.

Ultimately, Qualcomm had three major findings with their successful validation testing. The first, of course, being that this worked at all, proving that it can be done. Meanwhile in regards to performance, Qualcomm measured their HBC solution as delivering more than five-times the energy efficiency (on a bandwidth-per-watt basis) than HBM4 as per its own specifications. Finally, while the company is not disclosing specific bandwidth figures, they are categorizing the measured bandwidth at 18x higher than external LPDDR5X.

The energy efficiency figure in particular is a bit short of Qualcomm’s initial projections for the technology, where they were hoping to beat HBM by 6x. But if this carries over to a full product, it still represents a significant improvement in efficiency.

According to Qualcomm, their validation testing also includes the thermal behaviors of the product, though the company has not gone into any further detail there. Qualcomm has had little to say on the subject so far, but thermal considerations are one of the major technical hurdles they will need to overcome, as a more active compute die as the base die in a stacked memory architecture is expected to put out more heat.

With their initial HBC validation complete, Qualcomm is now looking at moving on to the next step of commercialization of the technology with their Dragonfly AI250 accelerator. The successor to the Dragonfly AI200 accelerator due this year, AI250 will be the first product to integrate HBC – and it will be a key part of future Qualcomm AI accelerators after that. AI250 does not have a launch date yet, but according to Qualcomm it will begin sampling in H1 of this year, which is potentially a move-up for the company’s plans following the initial announcement that sampling would take place earlier this year.

If everything pans out with HBC, the technology will not be limited to Dragonfly AI accelerators, either. Qualcomm has previously announced that they would also be bringing the technology to their consumer-focused Snapdragon products – though the company is not specifying when and what products at the time.

Ultimately, HBC is a play for energy efficiency and a lower TCO for Qualcomm. If the technology pans out, the company expects to be able to deliver AI inference accelerators that are both more energy efficient and cheaper to build than contemporary designs. Which in turn would make them cheaper to operate (and ideally, cheaper to acquire) than GPUs for large AI inference operations. We will get to see how that plays out over the coming months as Qualcomm moves towards sampling Dragonfly AI250 in the first half of next year.

articles.title: Liquid-Cooled NVIDIA Servers at the ASRock Rack OCP 2026 Booth
articles.summary: We checked out the ASRock Rack booth at OCP 2026 and saw servers ranging from fully integrated NVIDIA NVL72 racks to liquid-cooled switches The post Liquid-Cooled NVIDIA Servers at the ASRock Rack OCP 2026 Booth appeared first on ServeTheHome .
bodyEvidence: At OCP Global Summit 2026 in San Jose, we stopped by the ASRock Rack booth and saw a broad set of NVIDIA systems. That included a full NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 rack. Next to it were HGX Rubin NVL8 servers in both 2U and 5U, two NVIDIA MGX RTX PRO servers, and a dual NVIDIA Vera CPU server. We also spotted the liquid-cooled NVIDIA Spectrum-X SN6600-LD switch and the passively cooled NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPU.
A big theme was liquid cooling. ASRock Rack used direct-to-chip liquid cooling on its rack-scale system and HGX servers, including an 8x RTX PRO 6000 PCIe server.

The XGMRACK-VR/NVL72 is ASRock Rack’s version of the NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72. It is a 48RU NVIDIA MGX rack with a 5000A busbar and a liquid manifold. Inside are 18 Vera Rubin compute trays and nine NVLink 6 switch trays, for a total of 36 NVIDIA Vera CPUs and 72 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs.

NVIDIA lists the full rack at 3,600 PFLOPS of NVFP4 inference (sparse) and 2,520 PFLOPS of NVFP4 training (dense). It has 20.7TB of HBM4, and each Rubin GPU gets 288GB. Power comes from four 3RU 19″ power shelves. Each shelf is rated at 110kW and uses six 18.3kW PSUs plus bulk capacitors. ASRock Rack offers in-rack, in-row, RDHx, or liquid-to-air sidecar CDU options.

Each compute tray is a 1U NVIDIA MGX design with two Vera Rubin Superchips. Each Superchip connects two Rubin GPUs to one Vera CPU over NVLink-C2C. Networking is eight 800Gbps OSFP ports from NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, plus two 400Gbps QSFP112 ports from an NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPU. There are even management switches up top for the lower-speed networking.
The trays are fully liquid-cooled, which helps lower the total power consumption in the rack, and is something that NVIDIA has been advancing along with its partners for a few generations now.
For those who want a more traditional HGX 8-GPU form factor, there were options for that as well, but with a twist.

The 2U16X-GNR2/DLC RUBIN was one of the most impressive systems at the booth. It puts an NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 board, with eight Rubin GPUs, into a 2U chassis. It is fully liquid-cooled, covering the E1.S drives, CPUs, and GPUs, with no fans. Networking includes NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs and BlueField-4 DPUs. Power comes in over a 54V DC busbar.

The host is a dual-socket Intel Xeon 6 platform. It supports the Xeon 6700P, 6500P, and 6700E series in LGA 4710 sockets, with 16+16 DIMM slots at 2DPC. While it supports other series, given the cost of the rest of the system, we would imagine the vast majority of folks buying these will opt for the Xeon 6700P series.
There are eight 800Gbps OSFP ports via NVIDIA ConnectX-9, along with 8x hot-swap E1.S NVMe bays. NVIDIA quotes 400 PFLOPS of NVFP4 compute (sparse) for HGX Rubin NVL8.
The HGX 8-GPU platform underwent major changes in this generation, including a change in GPU orientation in the tray. This change enables it to work in high-density, liquid-cooled racks.
There was more in the booth, including hybrid-cooled servers, so let us get to those next.

articles.title: NVIDIA Updates Rubin GPU Specs as First Production Hardware Arrives
articles.summary: As production hardware starts shipping, NVIDIA has updated some of the specifications for its Rubin GPU platforms The post NVIDIA Updates Rubin GPU Specs as First Production Hardware Arrives appeared first on ServeTheHome .
bodyEvidence: As we roll into the fourth quarter of 2026, NVIDIA and its partners are in the middle of the Vera Rubin ramp-up, including hyperscalers making some of the first NVL72 systems generally available to their customers . With Vera Rubin reaching the tipping point of its production roll-out, NVIDIA is also finally locking down the hardware shipping specifications. As it turns out, the company has quietly revised those specifications, with the Rubin GPU now offering less memory and scale-up networking (NVLink) bandwidth than NVIDIA previously promoted, but more scale-out bandwidth.

As initially spotted by IT Home , back in September NVIDIA posted the updated specifications for its Rubin GPU and various Rubin-based products on their webpages and in NVIDIA’s architecture datasheet. To be sure, it is not unusual for server hardware specifications to change before a product’s launch, especially for something like Vera Rubin, which was announced nearly a year in advance. NVIDIA’s case is no different, with the company previously noting that those specifications were preliminary and that “all values are up to and subject to change” at the time.

First, let us talk about NVIDIA’s Rubin GPU. The cornerstone of NVIDIA’s ambitions for this generation, NVIDIA’s Rubin server GPU will find its way into systems big and small and serve as the building block for much larger projects.

Compared to NVIDIA’s preliminary specifications, the HBM4 memory bandwidth for a single Rubin GPU has been revised down notably. NVIDIA was initially targeting 22TB/second of memory bandwidth per Rubin GPU. At 8 stacks of HBM4 memory, that meant running each stack at about 10.75Gbps/pin. But with these revised shipping specifications, a single Rubin GPU will now provide 19.2TB/second of bandwidth, for a data rate of about 9.375Gbps/pin, a net loss of 1.375Gbps, or roughly 11%.

This spec change comes as NVIDIA has been projecting some very aggressive data rates for HBM4. The super-sized version of the high-bandwidth memory specification already doubled the memory bus width per stack from 1024 bits to 2048 bits. At the same time, the official specification called for HBM4 stacks to run at a slightly lower clock rate than HBM3E, targeting 8Gbps/pin. NVIDIA’s 10.75Gbps rate was significantly higher than the original HBM4 specification, and even their newly reduced 9.375Gbps data rate is still quite a bit above.

For context, NVIDIA’s rival AMD will run its HBM4 stacks on the MI455X at only 7.6Gbps/pin . So NVIDIA’s revised targets are significantly higher than those of some other HBM4 consumers. Even after the news broke, NVIDIA has not said why it revised the memory bandwidth specs down. In lieu of that, the immediate assumption is that NVIDIA and its memory partners cannot deliver on those specs, be it memory controller speeds, memory stack speeds, memory stack yields (how many can run at the desired speed), or perhaps a combination of all of those factors. Regardless of the reason, the net result is that customers will have less GPU memory bandwidth at their disposal, with performance ramifications.

NVLink interconnect bandwidth is also taking a hit compared to NVIDIA’s original expectations. The preliminary specification for NVIDIA’s multi-GPU connection and scale-up fabric was for 3.6TB/second of NVLink bandwidth for each Rubin GPU. That is now a flat 3.0TB/second, a 600GB/second (or 17%) reduction. NVLink is an area where NVIDIA pushes hard to make many physical GPUs act as one, so it usually pushes the limits of what is possible.

While NVLink (scale-up) bandwidth has been reduced, scale-out networking bandwidth is now overperforming. For a single Rubin GPU, NVIDIA is offering 450GB/second of networking bandwidth, up from their preliminary specification of 400GB/second.

Beyond these changes, NVIDIA has not changed any other specifications for Rubin GPUs. The theoretical (on paper) compute throughput remains unchanged at 50 PFLOPS of FP4 inference and 35 PFLOPS of FP4 training. So NVIDIA has hit its clock speed and memory-capacity targets for the GPU.

Rubin’s spec changes will also affect all the products it will go into, most notably NVIDIA’s flagship Vera Rubin NVL72 rack. NVL72 showcases all of NVIDIA’s technologies, integrating its Vera CPUs, BlueField-4 DPUs, and, of course, Rubin GPUs.

For NVL72, its specifications have been revised in lockstep with the changes to a single Rubin GPU. That means that cumulative GPU memory bandwidth has gone from 1,580TB/second to 1400TB/second for the rack-scale system, a net loss of 180 TB (11%). Though, as with a single Rubin, the GPU memory capacity for NVL72 remains unchanged at 20.7TB of HBM4.

NVLink bandwidth across the system for its scale-up domain has also been adjusted. NVIDIA’s plans to offer 260TB/second of bandwidth across the rack have been revised down to 216TB/second, a 17% reduction matching the new 3TB/second rate of each Rubin GPU.

The silver lining for NVL72 is that it gets the same scale-out networking bandwidth boost as the individual Rubin chips. So whereas NVL72 was originally slated to offer 28.8TB/second of networking bandwidth, that has been dialed up to 32.4TB/second (bidirectional). This means that for larger deployments that make heavy use of scale-out networking, more bandwidth (and ideally, more performance) is now available than NVIDIA first projected.

Past this, the rest of the figures for Vera Rubin NVL72 remain unchanged from the earlier specifications. Whether an NVL72 rack can hit quite the same level of AI performance with less memory and NVLink bandwidth as originally intended seems doubtful, but the GPU compute hardware (and its CPU counterpart) is shipping at spec.

Finally, separate from the specification changes to the base Rubin GPU and the NVL72 rack, NVIDIA has also revised its other products built from Rubin. This includes the Vera Rubin Superchip, the Vera Rubin NVL4, and the HGX Rubin NVL8 products. The last one is getting a special mention here because, on top of the Rubin spec changes, it is getting a further change of its own.

On top of GPU memory bandwidth and NVLink bandwidth reductions, NVIDIA is also cutting back the amount of HBM4 memory available in NVL8 systems. These systems were originally set to come with 2.3TB of HBM4, but that is now down to a flat 2.0TB, losing 300GB (or 13%) of GPU memory.

NVIDIA’s preliminary figure would require each Rubin GPU in an NVL8 to be a full Rubin with its complete complement of 288GB of HBM4 available. However, a 2.0TB setup means each GPU needs only around 250GB of HBM4 available. That, in turn, requires only 7 of the GPU’s 8 HBM4 memory stacks.

Consequently, NVL8 is taking the biggest memory bandwidth hit of the entire Rubin family. Rather than losing just 11% of its memory bandwidth, it is losing 26%, or about 46TB/second. Each Rubin GPU would only have 250GB to 252GB of memory available, for 16.8TB/second of bandwidth per GPU.

Inference performance remains unchanged, at 400 PFLOPS for FP4, but FP4 training performance has been reduced from 280 PFLOPS to 270, and FP8 training has similarly been dialed down from 140 PFLOPS to 130. The 8-way Rubin systems do get the same network bandwidth improvement as the rest of the Rubin lineup. That figure has gone from 1.6TB/second to 1.8TB/second.

Finally, these changes affect both versions of the HGX NVL8, as well as DGX systems based on the NVL8 platform. Both the HGX Rubin NVL8 (Rubin + x86 CPU) and the HGX Vera Rubin NVL8 (Rubin + Vera) are subject to the same GPU changes.

It seems NVIDIA has had to rein in its ambitions for the Rubin GPU to bring the product to market at the scale they are aiming for, dialing back both GPU HBM4 memory bandwidth and NVLink networking bandwidth. The full ramifications of these changes are unclear at this time since not all workloads are bottlenecked by memory or networking bandwidth in the same way. In some respects, it is academic, since these changes apply to all shipping Rubin hardware from day one. Still, there will be a lot of NVIDIA Rubin deployed over the next few quarters.

bodyEvidence: What do you actually need to keep running when the power goes out? For most households, the fridge, wifi, phones, and a few other essentials come first. Buying enough battery storage for every appliance in the house can come later – and that’s the appeal of BLUETTI’s latest launch, the Apex 200 portable power station .

The Apex 200 starts with 2.56kWh of storage and 3.2kW of continuous AC output, with the option to add batteries when you need longer backup. Built-in RV connections also mean it can earn its keep between blackouts.
BLUETTI launches the Apex 200 on November 4, with standalone super early-bird pricing starting at $1,099 through November 18 . Electrek readers can get an extra 5% off with code ELECTREK5OFF .
Here’s how to work out which setup is worth buying for your home or RV.
The Apex 200 takes the expandable design of BLUETTI’s flagship Apex series and puts it in a smaller package.
You get a 2,560Wh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery. The 3.2kW of continuous AC output increases to 3.6kW when an expansion battery is connected or the unit is actively charging.
The enclosure holds all that in 36.2 liters and weighs 26.9kg (59.3 lb). You’ll want two hands to move it, but it’s convenient to move it between home and your camper.

BLUETTI’s UltraCell technology delivers an industry-leading energy density of 70.7 Wh/L, yet the Apex 200 is more than 50% smaller by volume than class competitors. For an RV owner, that smaller footprint frees up room for other gear.

A rough runtime calculation is: Usable battery capacity in watt-hours ÷ average load in watts = hours of operation.

With AC output on and the display off, idle consumption drops to just 10.5W.

bodyEvidence: A new car affordability crisis and punishing gas prices are driving an unprecedented number of used car buyers to consider going electric, and that increased demand without a corresponding increase in supply means these used EVs are flying off dealer lots.

Days on the lot. That’s dealer-speak for the average number of days a given vehicle typically sits in inventory before finding a buyer. That’s critically important to dealers, since the vehicles on their lots are commonly financed through something called floorplan credit, and every additional day a car spends on a dealer’s lot can mean another day of interest payments and another day closer to a curtailment . Days on the lot can be even more important to dealers when it comes to cars owned outright, as well, as the dealers can have significant cash tied up in vehicles they’ve purchased outright, and every day those cars sit is another day that money isn’t working for them elsewhere.
That’s what makes this month’s fastest-selling used EVs particularly interesting, because these used EVs aren’t just selling fast for electric vehicles – they’re selling fast, period .

Dealer news sources Automotive News and Cox Automotive report that the average new car spent 82 days on the lot in October, with a 75-day target being an industry-wide benchmark. At the same time, the Audi Q4 Sportback e-tron Quattro with its 258-mile EPA-estimated range is turning in just 29.8 days. (!)

That Audi’s not alone. In a recently-released vehicle pricing study , iSeeCars reported that the Toyota BZ4x , Lexus RZ300e , Honda Prologue , and Borrás-family favorite Polestar 2 are all turning in an average of 35 days or less, with the BMW i4, iX , Kia EV6 , and Chevrolet Equinox EV just a day or two behind.

“The results reveal a market where EVs are appreciating in average asking price much faster than other drivetrains, while also spending less time waiting for buyers,” said iSeeCars Executive Analyst Karl Brauer, who found that average transaction prices for EVs rose 9.8% last month as ICE-powered vehicles stayed steady, rising just 0.3%. “Hybrids are experiencing moderate improvements in price and selling speed, while gasoline-powered vehicles have seen their selling times increase,” he adds, “despite relatively stable prices.”
Used electric vehicles averaged a price of $32,533 in September 2026, up $2,896 from the $29,637 ATP recorded a year earlier.

articles.title: First: Volvo CE Electric equipment does the work, without disturbing the wildlife
articles.summary: For the first time, electric equipment assets are being put to work in the National Wildlife Refuge System, where a battery-powered, zero-emission ECR25 Electric compact excavator and L25 Electric compact wheel loader made by Volvo CE are making the wild more accessible to everyone. more…
bodyEvidence: For the first time, electric equipment assets are being put to work in the National Wildlife Refuge System, where a battery-powered, zero-emission ECR25 Electric compact excavator and L25 Electric compact wheel loader made by Volvo CE are making the wild more accessible to everyone.

Construction work isn’t exactly welcome in the wilderness – between diesel exhaust, engine noises, and the constant rumble of heavy machinery, even a relatively small project can have a big impact on the native wildlife. To minimize that impact, US Fish and Wildlife Service is turning to Volvo CE and its compact excavators and wheel loaders to get the job done, building out a new, ADA accessible trail in Virginia’s Occoquan Bay National Wildlife Refuge.

“We are excited to partner with the US Fish and Wildlife Service on this project to demonstrate Volvo’s commitment to lowering emissions and working to build the future we all want and need,” said Dr. Ray Gallant, VP of Product Management and Productivity, Volvo CE. “Projects like the one at the Occoquan Bay National Wildlife Refuge give a glimpse of how electric machines can create a more climate-friendly future for the construction industry.”

The refuge is home to a diverse array of grasslands, wetlands, and woods that attract red foxes, painted turtles, osprey, river otters, and countless other rarely seen species – and the ADA accessible path being laid down by the L25 Electric compact wheel loader will allow wheelchair-bound visitors to travel a half-mile-long trail around one of the pond . Meanwhile, the ECR25 Electric compact excavator will be digging trenches to improve drainage from the pond and helping to place a viewing platform that extends out over the water.
Keeping the machines running is a portable EV ARC solar-powered charging system from Beam Global that’s designed to drive down the project’s carbon footprint even further.

articles.title: GM is recalling more than 67,000 Cadillac and Chevy EVs over a brake software defect
articles.summary: General Motors (GM) issued a recall affecting more than 67,000 Cadillac and Chevy EVs because a software glitch can cause a temporary loss of braking. more…
bodyEvidence: General Motors (GM) issued a recall affecting more than 67,000 Cadillac and Chevy EVs because a software glitch can cause a temporary loss of braking.
The recall comes after a 2024 Cadillac Lyriq ran into a garage (at a low speed). On April 10, 2026, a GM tech expert submitted a report to GM’s Speak Up for Safety (SUFS) program for review.

After internal testing, GM was able to replicate the glitch, similar to a recall it issued in 2024. GM said the issue stems from a software glitch with the brake system control module (BSCM) that can cause a temporary loss of braking while driving under certain conditions.
When drivers lightly tap the brakes during a sharp turn and the vehicle hits a bump, the software’s slip calculation may misinterpret wheel movement.
In some instances, it can lead to a temporary loss of braking. The glitch only affects pAWD vehicles, including certain Cadillac Lyriq, Celestiq, Vistiq, and Chevy Blazer EV.
In a letter sent to the NHTSA on October 29, GM said the recall impacted 67,380 vehicles total, including certain:
According to documents filed with the NHTSA, GM found 24 field complaints related to the issue. Of these, 20 involved minor accidents, and two involved allegations of minor injuries.
The complaints were received between February 24, 2024, and June 11, 2026. GM said it has implemented software corrections in production over the past few months.
GM will update the BSCM software via an over-the-air (OTA) update or through a dealer, free of charge.

Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed out on December 14, 2026. In the meantime, you can contact Cadillac’s customer service at 1-800-333-4223 or Chevrolet’s customer service at 1-800-222-1020. GM’s recall number is N262570900.
You can also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 or visit the nhtsa.gov website for more information. The NHTSA campaign number is 26V717.

We also know the Fathom will have an NACS port after a prototype was caught at a Tesla Supercharger a few months ago.

articles.title: Germany’s EV share hits record 37% as BEVs beat gas and diesel combined
articles.summary: Battery-electric cars took a record 37% of Germany’s new car market in October, according to data released today by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA), the country’s federal motor vehicle authority. That’s 94,086 BEVs, up 79.5% from 52,425 a year earlier. For the second month in a row, German buyers registered more fully electric cars than gasoline and diesel cars combined. And with two months left in the year, Germany has already blown past the auto industry’s EV forecast for all of 2026. more…
bodyEvidence: Battery-electric cars took a record 37% of Germany’s new car market in October, according to data released today by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA), the country’s federal motor vehicle authority. That’s 94,086 BEVs, up 79.5% from 52,425 a year earlier.

For the second month in a row, German buyers registered more fully electric cars than gasoline and diesel cars combined. And with two months left in the year, Germany has already blown past the auto industry’s EV forecast for all of 2026.
The overall market barely grew in October. Total new car registrations rose 1.7% to 254,492 units, which means the EV growth came straight out of combustion cars.

Gasoline car registrations crashed 40.5% to 38,516 units, a 15.1% share. Diesel fell 21.6% to 23,882 units, or 9.4% of the market. Add them up and pure combustion cars made up just 24.5% of new registrations, 12.5 points less than BEVs alone.

Plug-in hybrids slipped 7.9% to 28,499 units (11.2%). So plug-ins accounted for about 48% of the German market last month, and the average CO2 emissions of new cars dropped 21.1% year-over-year to 79.4 g/km.

As we reported this summer, BEVs became the most popular powertrain in Germany for the first time in June with a 28.4% share. They’ve kept climbing every month since: 32.4% in August, 34.5% in September, and now 37% in October.

Through the first ten months of the year, Germany has registered 698,230 BEVs, up 60.7% year-over-year. That’s about 28.2% of the 2,476,290 new cars registered in 2026 so far, up from roughly 19% for the full year 2025.

And the industry didn’t see it coming. In December, the VDA, Germany’s auto industry association, forecast about 693,000 BEV registrations for all of 2026. Germany passed that in October. At the current pace, it’s on track for somewhere around 875,000 by the end of the year.

The biggest driver is Germany’s new EV incentive, which applies retroactively to cars registered since January 1. It pays €3,000 for a new BEV, bought or leased, and up to €6,000 for lower-income households with children. Households with taxable income above €80,000 (€90,000 with kids) don’t qualify.

The program targets private buyers, and that’s exactly where the KBA data shows the jump. Private registrations rose 20.6% in October, while commercial registrations fell 8.2%. Private buyers now make up 40.7% of the market.

Germany has been here before. The government killed its previous EV incentive overnight in December 2023, and BEV sales fell off a cliff in 2024. This time, the money is going to the buyers who need it most, and it’s moving the needle fast.

Tesla’s German numbers swing wildly with its quarterly delivery cycle. In September, the end of the quarter, it registered 12,552 cars (+268.7%) and the Model Y was the best-selling car in Germany. In October, it registered only 2,932, which is still up 290.9% but from a tiny base, for a 1.2% market share.

Year-to-date, Tesla is up 206.1% to 47,742 registrations. That’s a big rebound from a terrible 2025, but BYD is now slightly ahead with 47,961 (+216.1%). BYD registered 5,173 cars in October (+54.3%), though the majority of its German sales are plug-in hybrids, not BEVs.

The other Chinese brands are growing even faster. Leapmotor registered 3,661 cars in October, up 288.6%, and is at 19,705 for the year. Xpeng was up 284.4% to 1,380 units, and SAIC’s MG was up 48.5% to 4,140.

Volkswagen Group still owns the top of the EV charts, though. Through September, the Skoda Elroq was Germany’s best-selling EV with 30,845 units, ahead of the Tesla Model Y (29,464) and the VW ID.3 (24,352).
The EV boom is happening during one of the worst years in the history of Germany’s auto industry.

In October, the VW brand’s German registrations fell 4%, Audi dropped 8.4%, Porsche lost 5.7%, and Opel crashed 24.1%. BMW was flat (+0.1%), and Mercedes was the exception, up 8.5%. VW is still by far the biggest brand in Germany with an 18.2% share, but it’s down 5.6% for the year.

Last week, Volkswagen Group reported a €5.9 billion operating loss for the third quarter , its biggest quarterly loss since Dieselgate, driven by a writedown of its Porsche stake, weak sales in China, and thin EV margins. The group has already approved a plan to cut 100,000 jobs and close several German plants. Mercedes cut its 2026 car margin guidance to 2-3% last week, mainly because of China.
It’s not a product problem. VW’s new ID. Polo is sold out with over 30,000 orders , BMW has over 50,000 orders for the Neue Klasse iX3 , and the Elroq leads the German EV market.

Germany is proving what we’ve been saying for years. Give buyers EVs they can actually afford, and they switch fast. Fully electric cars went from about 19% of the market last year to 37% in October, and the country beat the industry’s full-year forecast with two months to spare. That’s not a slow transition.

One thing to consider when talking about EVs not being Germany-made is that Germany car makers can't make them fast enough. A lot of the models are sold out for months. It's not an excuse but something to keep in mind.
Compare that with North America, where EV sales dropped 44% after the US killed its federal EV tax credit. Same technology, sometimes the same cars. The difference is policy.
Germany’s problem is who’s capturing the demand. Hint: it’s not German automakers.

But whose fault is that? You can’t spend years dragging your feet on electrification and lobby government back and forth on EV incentives and then complain when those who are all-in on EVs are able to take better advantage of the customer shift amid another oil crisis.

articles.title: BYD’s new luxury electric SUV has one big problem: It weighs over 8,200 lbs
articles.summary: BYD’s new full-size electric SUV, the Denza N9 EV, was revealed in a regulatory filing, weighing in at over 8,200 lbs (3,760 kg). That creates one issue. more…
bodyEvidence: BYD’s new full-size electric SUV, the Denza N9 EV, was revealed in a regulatory filing, weighing in at over 8,200 lbs (3,760 kg). That creates one issue.
The Denza N9 first went on sale last March, a flagship plug-in hybrid (PHEV) SUV with a combined CLTC range of about 807 miles (1,300 km) on a full charge and full tank of gas.

BYD introduced the updated Flash Charging version earlier this year, which uses its second-generation Blade Batteries and delivers a pure electric CLTC range of 260 miles (420 km). Combined, it gets up to 944 miles (1,520 km) under CLTC conditions.
In the latest batch of new energy vehicles (NEVs) approved for sale by China’s MIIT (Ministry of Information Technology) this week, a new all-electric Denza N9 appeared.
The filing revealed the Denza N9 EV will be available with three electric motors, delivering a combined output of 1,193 horsepower (890 kW).
A badge on the back reveals it will use BYD’s tri-motor e3 platform. The setup features a single 362 horsepower (270 kW) front motor and two 415 horsepower (310 kW) rear electric motors.

The electric version measures 5,270 mm long, 2,030 mm wide, and 1,830 mm tall, with a 3,125 mm wheelbase, which is the same as the current Denza N9 PHEV Flash Charging model. It will be available in five- and six-seat configurations.
While the filing reveals it will use a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery with cells from BYD’s battery unit, FinDreams, it does not provide specifics like capacity or driving range.
One relatively big thing to note: the Denza N9 EV has a gross weight of 3,760 kg, or about 8,289 lbs.

Obscene weight , and that applies to other SUVs as well. Vehicle registration taxes should be based on vehicle weight as it wears out roads and endangers other road users and infrastructure and wastes resources.
As AutoNext points out, this makes it too heavy for an EU category B driving license, which covers up to 3,500 kg (7,716 lbs).
Last year, the EU updated the rules , allowing drivers who have held a category B license for two years to drive alternative-fuelled vehicles with a maximum weight of up to 4,250 kg (9,369 lbs).
While the Denza N9 EV would qualify as listed, newer drivers would still need a commercial EU category C1 driving license to drive it.
BYD launched its luxury sub-brand, Denza, in Europe and the UK in March, starting with the Z9 GT and the D9 van. More recently, it introduced the Bao 5 PHEV SUV and the Denza Z electric supercar.

articles.title: Xiaomi’s humanoid robots work a full 8-hour shift in its EV factory
articles.summary: Xiaomi has released footage of its humanoid robots working a full 8-hour shift at its EV factory, sorting center console side covers for its cars. The company says the robots did it on their own, catching and fixing their own mistakes along the way. If that’s fully autonomous, it’s truly impressive. But we’ve been disappointed by humanoid robot demos before, and Xiaomi left out the numbers that would let anyone check. more…
bodyEvidence: Xiaomi has released footage of its humanoid robots working a full 8-hour shift at its EV factory, sorting center console side covers for its cars. The company says the robots did it on their own, catching and fixing their own mistakes along the way.
If that’s fully autonomous, it’s truly impressive. But we’ve been disappointed by humanoid robot demos before, and Xiaomi left out the numbers that would let anyone check.

Xiaomi Tech posted the video on X on November 3, as the company picked up awards at the World Internet Conference in Wuzhen. It shows the robots pulling side covers from bins, carrying them to storage racks, and placing them into slots, with a running clock of cumulative working time and an “Autonomous, 100x Speed” label in the corner.

8 hours on the production line. 🤖 Xiaomi’s full-size humanoid robot takes on an 8-hour task at the Center Console Side-Cover Sorting Workstation at Xiaomi Auto Factory. Beyond sustained operation, it can autonomously detect and correct anomalies while coordinating with the… pic.twitter.com/brpO3S5bCn

According to Xiaomi, the robot covered the full day of production needs at that workstation. The company says it detected and corrected anomalies on its own and coordinated with the production line’s control system, calling it “another step toward real-world industrial deployment.”

This is the third milestone in a program Xiaomi has been running in public all year. In March, it put a humanoid in its Beijing EV factory as an “intern” installing self-tapping nuts. Xiaomi reported a 90.2% success rate over three hours, fast enough to meet the station’s 76-second cycle time. By July, it said that success rate was up to 98%, and it added two harder stations, including the side-cover sorting job from this week’s video.
Last December, Xiaomi’s CEO, Lei Jun, said the company plans to deploy humanoid robots in large numbers across its factories within five years.

Xiaomi also announced that its open-source Xiaomi-Robotics-1 AI model, pre-trained on 100,000 hours of real-world robot data, has started trial runs in Xiaomi staff apartments. In a 30-minute run, it completed more than 50 task chains across three rooms.

Xiaomi didn’t say how many parts the robots sorted, what the success rate was over eight hours, or how many times a human had to step in. It also didn’t explain how the robots stayed powered for a full shift: swapped batteries, a tether, or charging breaks.

And that matters, because “autonomous” in a robot video can mean anything. Tesla’s Optimus robots at the 2024 “We, Robot” event were remotely operated by humans , which Tesla didn’t disclose at the time. Last December, an Optimus took a suspicious tumble in a Miami demo , raising its hands to its head like a teleoperator pulling off a VR headset as it fell.

To be fair to Xiaomi, it has published success rates and cycle times for its earlier factory tests. That’s more than Tesla has ever shared about Optimus doing useful work, and Tesla now says it won’t deliver Optimus to outside customers until late 2027 .

The most interesting moment in the video comes around the 1:37 mark. In a segment Xiaomi labels “Dropped Material: Multi-Robot Collaboration,” a humanoid upper body mounted on a wheeled base rolls in to help the two legged robots.

It’s not the only thing on wheels in that scene, either. The bins of parts are shuttled around by autonomous mobile robots, the same kind of wheeled platforms that have been moving materials in car factories for years.

Wheels are the most efficient form of moving, but biology has prevented evolution of providing that to life forms because rotating "limbs" around an axis cannot provide for blood vessels, nerves and muscle attachments to feed and drive it. It took human ingenuity to discover it.

If this demo was truly fully autonomous for eight hours, with the robots handling their own errors, that’s one of the more impressive humanoid demos we’ve seen. Xiaomi deserves credit for putting its robots on a real production line and publishing some real numbers along the way. But we’ve been burned by “autonomous” robot demos before, so we’ll wait for more details before getting too excited.

The wheeled robot is our favorite part of the video, though. It’s a great example of why you shouldn’t bet everything on the humanoid form factor. Wheels are far more efficient than legs on most terrain, and a flat factory floor is the best-case scenario for wheels. A wheeled base doesn’t burn energy just to stay upright, it’s more stable when carrying parts, it has room for a much bigger battery (which would solve that 8-hour power question), and it needs fewer expensive actuators.

The value in these robots is in the hands, arms, and the AI driving them. Legs make sense in homes with stairs, and maybe that’s where Xiaomi wants to take them eventually. But factories were designed around carts and forklifts, not people walking around carrying parts.

articles.title: Puerto Rico tapped Sunrun’s home batteries for 18 straight days
articles.summary: Sunrun has doubled participation in its Puerto Rico virtual power plant to more than 60,000 customers, and the grid is putting those home batteries to work: It tapped into them for 18 straight days in October. more…
bodyEvidence: Sunrun has doubled participation in its Puerto Rico virtual power plant to more than 60,000 customers, and the grid is putting those home batteries to work: It tapped into them for 18 straight days in October.
A virtual power plant (VPP) connects batteries across thousands of properties and coordinates them to supply power together.

Sunrun says its VPP network in Puerto Rico now includes nearly 70,000 batteries, frequently delivering 45 megawatts (MW) for four hours at a time. It has dispatched them more than 60 times since April, including daily deployments beginning October 13 during unusually hot weather.

For Puerto Ricans, who pay some of the highest electricity prices in the US, getting reliable power for all that money remains a problem. Residential electricity averaged 26.36 cents per kilowatt-hour in August, compared with a US average of 18.16 cents, according to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA).

That makes the batteries already installed at homes pretty useful. The grid can pay to tap their stored energy when supplies get tight, putting existing equipment to work without waiting for a new power plant to be built.
Sunrun’s network grew from around 4,000 customers in 2024 to more than 30,000 in 2025. It says it’s the largest aggregator in Puerto Rico’s Customer Battery Energy Sharing (CBES) program.

LUMA, the island’s grid operator, calls on CBES when it expects electricity demand or reserve needs to exceed available generation. Companies such as Sunrun then manage the battery response automatically.

Homeowners get paid for sharing energy and choose how much to keep for backup. Sunrun says most share a small portion of their total battery capacity; the company earns recurring revenue for operating the network.
Across the wider CBES program, LUMA reported in July that more than 90,000 participating customers had helped provide an average of 75 MW during generation shortfalls.
Puerto Rico’s reliability problem goes well beyond hurricanes.

Customers averaged 36 hours without power in 2025, even excluding major events, according to the US EIA. That’s up 19% from 2024. Mainland US customers generally experience about two hours a year under the same measure. Major events added another 23 hours of outages on the island.

More batteries can help, but the size of the shortfall still matters. In an April regulatory filing , participating aggregators said the program couldn’t prevent every rolling blackout in 2025 because some supply gaps exceeded its roughly 50 MW of four-hour capacity. They’re looking to enroll more batteries so the program can cover larger shortfalls.

articles.title: Tesla accused of selling FSD to Korean owners who can’t legally use it
articles.summary: A South Korean consumer group is asking regulators to stop Tesla from marketing “Full Self-Driving” to customers whose cars can’t legally run it. By Tesla’s own numbers, that covers 99% of the Teslas it sold in Korea last year. Citizens United for Consumer Sovereignty plans to file the complaint with the Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) on Thursday, according to Reuters, which reviewed it. It comes just a week after a Seoul court threw out a refund lawsuit from Korean owners who paid for FSD. more…
bodyEvidence: A South Korean consumer group is asking regulators to stop Tesla from marketing “Full Self-Driving” to customers whose cars can’t legally run it. By Tesla’s own numbers, that covers 99% of the Teslas it sold in Korea last year.

Citizens United for Consumer Sovereignty plans to file the complaint with the Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) on Thursday, according to Reuters, which reviewed it. It comes just a week after a Seoul court threw out a refund lawsuit from Korean owners who paid for FSD.

It all comes down to where the car was built. The Model S, Model X, and Cybertruck come from US factories and enter Korea under the KORUS free trade agreement, which recognizes US safety standards. Those are the only Teslas that got “FSD (Supervised)” when Tesla switched it on in Korea late last year.
The problem is that those don’t represent the vast majority of Tesla vehicles sold in Korea.
The Model 3 and Model Y sold in Korea come from Giga Shanghai. There’s no equivalent deal with China, so those cars need Korean approval that FSD doesn’t have.

And that’s most of the fleet. Tesla Korea country manager Seo Young-deuk told lawmakers last month that FSD works on about 20% of Teslas registered in the country. Tesla has sold more than 170,000 Shanghai-built vehicles in Korea since 2023, per data it handed to the National Assembly, and sales of those China-made cars grew more than fivefold between 2023 and 2025.

Seo’s figure also clears up the conflicting eligibility numbers we flagged when Korean police booked 80 Tesla drivers for using illegal FSD unlock devices last month. A lawmaker’s data from May put it at 2.4%, while a data firm counted 20.7% in August. Tesla’s own testimony matches the higher one.
For years, Tesla charged Korean buyers a one-time 9.043 million won (about $6,726) for FSD. It moved to a 150,000 won ($112) monthly subscription in August.

The complaint points to Tesla’s “coming soon” promotion last year and a demo video shot on Korean roads. Neither made it clear that FSD would only work on a small slice of the cars Tesla was selling. The group says Tesla knew that and kept pitching the package to every buyer anyway.

“Tesla generated substantial revenue by selling an expensive driver-assistance system to mass-market buyers who cannot use it for even a single day,” said Choi Young-suk, who heads automotive issues at the group.
It wants the KFTC to temporarily order Tesla to stop marketing FSD for ineligible cars. It’s also asking for fines and for the case to be sent to state investigators.

The KFTC is already looking at this. An official told Reuters the agency opened a probe into Tesla’s FSD advertising earlier this year and has received written responses from the company. Tesla didn’t respond to Reuters’ requests for comment.

Tesla has collected FSD money from buyers of China-made cars in Korea for more than three years. But at an October 8 parliamentary hearing, Seo testified that Tesla had never formally asked the transport ministry to test FSD. Tesla filed for certification about two weeks later.

Approval won’t be a rubber stamp either. The ministry told a lawmaker that FSD doesn’t comply with local safety rules, including the requirement that drivers keep their hands on the wheel. Current FSD versions let drivers go hands-free as long as the cabin camera sees them watching the road.
None of this slowed sales. Tesla passed BMW this year to become Korea’s top imported car brand.

So far, owners haven’t had much luck in court. Last month, a Seoul court dismissed a lawsuit from Tesla owners seeking FSD refunds, with the judge pointing to Korean regulations, not Tesla, as the reason more features never launched.

articles.title: What does a blue Texas sweep mean for Elon Musk, Tesla & SpaceX?
articles.summary: After a historic election defeat in one of the most expensive elections in US election history, the state of Texas has turned blue. Along with this come potential implications for Elon Musk and his companies. more…
bodyEvidence: After a historic election defeat in one of the most expensive elections in US election history, the state of Texas has turned blue. Along with this come potential implications for Elon Musk and his companies.

The US midterm election was yesterday, and ended up in a stunning result, with Democrats taking control of both houses of Congress by wide margins, and flipping seats that had been considered safe around the nation.

Perhaps most notably, many of these seats were in Texas – a republican stronghold which saw a clean sweep, with the Democrats winning every statewide contest. Republicans maintained some state legislative power and won the State Senate, but as of this writing Democrats are currently ahead in the count for the State House.

The highest profile contest was for Texas Senate, where James Talarico won by a 55-43 margin. This race set the record for the most expensive Senate race in the nation’s history, with over half a billion dollars spent on this one seat alone.

About half of the total money spent on the race came courtesy of republican PACs, a method by which companies and the ultra-wealthy can launder money into bribes to buy elections. And most of the PAC money in the race came from one man, Elon Musk, who spent $212 million to support the enormously unpopular and scandal-ridden outgoing Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton
That’s nearly half of the $474 million dollars that Musk put into this election cycle, suggesting that he saw this race of particular importance. And yet, his candidate lost miserably.

But the rout did not stop with Paxton. Paxton’s old job as AG is now going to be filled by Democrat Nathan Johnson. And Greg Abbott, the outgoing Governor, was defeated by Gina Hinojosa. Even the less high-profile races for court seats were swept by Democrats – three seats on the 15th Court of Appeals and four seats on the Texas Supreme Court.
And those results, even beyond the big-spending Senate race, could all matter quite a lot to Elon Musk.
In 2021, Musk announced that Tesla would move its headquarters to Texas , after Musk got in a spat with California government because he didn’t want to follow COVID restrictions for worker safety.

But the move wasn’t only about COVID restrictions – it was also about Musk’s vision of having more control over the business environment. And, by making allies with Ken Paxton and Greg Abbott, he has had quite a bit of control in Texas.
The two have rolled out the red carpet for Musk, giving him carte blanche in his adopted state.

Autonomous vehicle regulations have been changed, allowing driverless Robotaxis to operate where other states with more advanced regulations and transparency requirements would not. And many other laws benefitting Tesla and SpaceX have been passed. Paxton even sued Sam Altman , Musk’s chief AI rival, just weeks ago.
Perhaps more notably for Musk personally, Texas has promised to allow Musk to get away with more financial shenanigans than states with more established business regulations might.

With Tesla both headquartered and incorporated in Texas, it can now use special “ business courts ” instituted by Abbott at Musk’s own urging. If cases from these courts are appealed, they go to the 15th Court of Appeals, a court created by Abbott and filled with 3 hand-picked judges, intended to reduce the chance that a Democratic district court (say, one in Austin, whereTesla is headquartered) gets final say on any issue.
But, the 15th Court of Appeals just had elections last night – and its three seats were flipped to Democratic control.

The 15th Court of Appeals also, just last week , stopped an inquiry into thousands of pages of emails between Abbott and Musk. The emails had been released , but are heavily redacted, with Abbott referring to the redacted portions as having “ intimate ” information in them.
And who made that request for inquiry into the emails? Gina Hinojosa, a name you might recognize, as she is the next Governor of Texas, as of last night.

As of yet, those emails have not all been released, so we don’t actually know exactly how much influence Musk was able to exercise over the state’s outgoing Governor. But given the changes we know about, the money Musk spent in Texas, and the thousands of pages of emails that have been redacted, it seems likely that there is something more to be found in them.
So what does this all mean for Tesla, our main area of coverage here at Electrek ?

On a Texas state level, probably not all that much. There’s no reason that Democrats in the state would interfere with Tesla’s production of electric vehicles – in fact, they’d probably encourage it more than republicans do. Talarico has stated that he supports Tesla – it is a large employer in the state, after all.

And certainly, the national wins by Democrats could be a boon for EVs, and for climate action , given how hostile republicans have been to them (and Musk has been the single largest supporter of that hostility towards EVs, which has cost Tesla billions ).

The same likely goes for SpaceX – perhaps a blue Texas will be more restrictive of the company’s improper usage of protected habitats , or building of data centers , or whatever the hell is going on on twitter . But the core businesses of space launches and Starlink don’t seem likely to go anywhere.

For Elon Musk, though, things could be different. Given his “intimate” relationship with Abbott, the extreme amounts of money he spent on Paxton, and the highly personal nature of his truly ridiculous attacks against Talarico, it seems unlikely that he will have a similar level of allyship with Texas government actors as he did in prior years. Talarico’s main anti-corruption message was seemingly aimed straight at Musk’s attempts to buy elections, after all.

And given his high levels of spending on a party that is outright hostile electric vehicles, it seems clear that his personal fortunes are far more important to him than the well-being of his companies.

as a texan, I had zero faith that talrico would win, especially with the amount of money musk dumped in the race at the last minute. I’m so heartened to see that money cannot buy everything and that we, as a country, are finally pushing back against the trump/musk insanity. maybe we can start upholding the constitution and ensuring the law applies to all citizens regardless of wealth.

This is all important to note, because Musk has been working towards a scheme to merge SpaceX and Tesla, a deal which would likely be a detriment to both companies and all of their shareholders . Musk wants the deal so he can exercise more control over, and extract more personal wealth from, the combined entity.
But that scheme could rely on a favorable legal environment in Texas courts, an environment that just got less favorable.

And, given Musk’s penchant for childish lashings-out anytime he deems people insufficiently obsequious to his imagined greatness, could we see another situation where Musk encounters the tiniest amount of pushback from state government and then picks up his toys and leaves, as he already did in both California and Delaware? Time will have to tell. Keep your popcorn buckets primed and ready.

articles.summary: BYD wasted no time, with sales of its new flagship electric sedan reaching 4,000 in just 19 days since its launch. more…
bodyEvidence: BYD wasted no time, with sales of its new flagship electric sedan reaching 4,000 in just 19 days since its launch.
With a record of more than 300,000 electric vehicles sold last month, BYD sold more EVs than the US did in the entire third quarter, combined.
A big part of the higher demand is thanks to BYD’s latest breakthrough technology, including its second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging technology.

BYD began equipping vehicles with the new battery and charging tech in March, and over the past six months it has posted higher year-over-year sales growth. Through October, BYD sold 1,953,700 vehicles, up 6% compared to the same period in 2025.
On October 13, BYD launched the Great Han, or “Da Han” in China, the first fully electric D-segment flagship sedan in its Dynasty lineup.
Just 19 days after its launch, BYD said Great Han EV sales reached 4,000 units. At that rate, sales could reach 10,000 or more in its first full month.
With “class-beating high value,” BYD said, “it has firmly established itself in the mid-to-high-end sedan segment above 250,000 yuan,” which is about $37,500.

The Great Han is available in three variants, priced from 235,900 yuan, or about $35,000. Buyers can choose from single- or dual-motor powertrains. The standard rear-wheel-drive (RWD) Premium trim offers up to 1,008 km (626 miles) of CLTC range, while the all-wheel-drive (AWD) Flagship variant offers up to 880 km (546 miles).
All models use a 102.326 kWh BYD Blade 2.0 battery pack. The RWD models have a single 370 kW (496 hp) motor, while the AWD variant adds a 200 kW (268 hp) front motor for a combined 570 kW (764 hp).
Like most of its new vehicles, the Great Han has a roof-mounted LiDAR and BYD’s God’s Eye B, a more advanced version of its intelligent driving system.
The ADAS system offers safety and convenience features, including Navigate on Autopilot on highways and in cities, plus remote autonomous parking.
All variants also include premium features, such as BYD’s DiSus-A dual-chamber air suspension system, rear-wheel steering, and zero-gravity front seats.

Measuring 5,256 mm in length, 1,999 mm in width, and 1,510 mm in height, with a 3,130 mm wheelbase, the Great Han is slightly bigger than the Tesla Model S and Lucid Air. It’s closer in size to the long-wheelbase Mercedes-Benz S-Class.
Thanks to BYD’s second-gen Blade Batteries and Flash Charging technology, the vehicle’s battery can charge from 10% to 70% in just 5 minutes. A full recharge (10% to 97%) takes just 9 minutes.

The Great Han joins the Great Tang SUV as the flagship sedan under BYD’s Dynasty lineup. BYD announced that Great Tang sales reached 14,000 units in October, marking four months of sales above 10,000.

articles.title: Pennsylvania is way ahead on NEVI charging – now comes another $37M
articles.summary: Pennsylvania is putting $37 million in federal NEVI funding toward what PennDOT says will be 515 new public EV charging ports across the Philadelphia region, including curbside chargers. more…
bodyEvidence: Pennsylvania is putting $37 million in federal NEVI funding toward what PennDOT says will be 515 new public EV charging ports across the Philadelphia region, including curbside chargers.
The awards cover Bucks, Chester, Delaware, Montgomery, and Philadelphia counties. PennDOT says the projects will expand public charging availability by 27% across the region and 53% in Philadelphia.
For drivers without a driveway, curbside charging gives them somewhere to plug in while parked near home.

It’s Electric PA received $2.93 million for 157 on-street Level 2 ports across 13 Philadelphia neighborhoods. Voltpost received funding for another 62 curbside ports across the four suburban counties.

Fast charging is getting funding, too. PositivEnergy received $7.2 million for 54 DC fast-charging ports at 11 Philadelphia Parking Authority lots. Tesla received two $392,000 awards for eight ports each at Royal Farms in Broomall and Wawa in Plymouth Meeting.

The money comes from the federal National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) program, created by the Biden administration’s Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. Pennsylvania’s five-year allocation is $171.5 million.

NEVI initially focused on fast charging along designated highway corridors. States can spend the money more broadly after the Federal Highway Administration certifies that their corridor charging requirements have been met. Pennsylvania received that certification on September 22, 2025.
In fact, Pennsylvania has built 54 EV charging stations using NEVI funds so far – more than double the number of any other state.

PennDOT’s community charging program supports both Level 2 and DC fast charging. Its published program minimum requirements include at least four ports per proposed station, at least 6 kW per port, two ADA-compliant parking spaces, and J1772 or CCS connectors on every port. Equipment must also meet Buy America requirements.
PennDOT lists 71 awards in this southeastern round as part of its roughly $100 million statewide community charging effort.
Applications for the western region close November 20. Central and eastern Pennsylvania applications close March 12, 2027.
thanks for posting. PA continues to lead the country in turning this program into actual chargers. The statewide coverage is night and day from just 2-3 years ago.

For the southeastern projects, PennDOT’s estimated schedule puts environmental reviews in November 2026 through January 2027, followed by agreement execution in January and February. Drivers will still have to wait for construction and commissioning before these awards become places to plug in.

bodyEvidence: The Hyundai IONIQ 5 remains one of America’s most popular EVs outside Tesla, with October sales up 21%.
While the Tesla Model Y and Model 3 still dominate the US electric vehicle market, accounting for about 50% of all sales through the third quarter , it was the Hyundai IONIQ 5 that ranked third.
The market has slowed since the $7,500 federal tax credit was removed last September, with several automakers reporting fewer EV sales than in 2025 when buyers rushed to claim the credit.
Hyundai responded by cutting prices on the 2026 IONIQ 5 by up to nearly $10,000 on some trims, with a new starting MSRP of around $35,000.
As the market shows signs of recovery, IONIQ 5 sales bounced back in October, rising 21% to 1,981 units.

While Hyundai sold only 169 IONIQ 9s last month (-47%), sales are still up 49% through October, with nearly 6,700 units sold.
Hyundai’s hybrids set a new October sales record, rising 20% from last year and accounting for 29% of total sales in October. Through October, Hyundai’s total US sales are up 3% YOY at 770,916 units.
Since not all automakers report monthly sales figures, it’s hard to determine where the IONIQ 5 stands through October.

Earlier today, Hyundai’s sister brand Kia reported that sales of its three-row electric SUV, the EV9, were up 11% year over year in October. EV9 sales are now up 5% year-to-date, with 13,835 units sold through October.

If you want more range, upgrading to the extended-range SE RWD model costs an extra $2,500, but you get up to 318 miles of range on a single charge.

articles.title: Volkswagen’s affordable ID. Polo wins German Car of the Year 2027 as EVs dominate
articles.summary: Volkswagen’s new ID. Polo took the overall title of “German Car of the Year 2027,” starting at just €24,995 ($28,000). more…
bodyEvidence: Volkswagen’s new ID. Polo took the overall title of “German Car of the Year 2027,” starting at just €24,995 ($28,000).

After winning in its class among entry-level models (up to €25,000), the VW ID. Polo beat out strong international competition to take the top spot as German Car of the Year for 2027 among all vehicles.
The Volkswagen Group has won two years in a row with a compact EV. Last year, it was the Skoda Elroq.

Volkswagen opened orders for the ID. Polo with the 52 kWh battery at the end of April. In July, it added the entry-level model with the 37 kWh battery, starting at just €24,995 ($28,000) with a WLTP range of up to 207 miles (334 km).
The Life and Style variants are also available with the 37 kWh battery, starting from €29,195 ($32,500).
With DC fast charging speeds of up to 90 kW, the ID. Polo with the 37 kWh battery can recharge from 10% to 80% in about 23 minutes.

The prestigious award “confirms what the ID. Polo stands for,” VW brand CEO Thomas Schäfer said. He added the entry-level EV “brings electric mobility to where it can make the greatest impact: right into people’s everyday lives.”
Since orders opened at the end of April, Schäfer said “well over 50,000 people have ordered their ID. Polo.”
As the first of what the company calls “a true Volkswagen again,” the ID. Polo is the first to bear an established name and the brand’s new Pure Positive design language.
The jury includes nearly 50 German and international auto journalists, and the award is considered one of the most prestigious in the industry.

The reason this class of vehicles is winning awards is that Europe buys a lot of B-segment vehicles (small hatchbacks) that aren't intended as city-only transport. Many families use them as their only vehicle.
And, up till now, there haven't been many BEVs available in that category.
It is compact, reasonably powerful, reasonably fast charging, acceptable charging rate, has good luggage capacity and feels nice to drive.

In other segments, electric cars swept the awards, with the Kia PV5 van winning in the compact class (€25,000 and €40,000), and Mercedes-Benz GLC Electric taking the top spot in the premium segment (€40,000 to €70,000). Hyundai’s electric sports car, the IONIQ 6 N, won German Performance Car 2027.
Martin Sander, the Group’s sales boss, said earlier this month the company is “seeing a significantly accelerated trend towards all-electric vehicles” in its home market.

VW Group’s Electric Urban Car Family has received nearly 150,000 orders after series production began in June. The lineup currently includes the VW ID. Polo and ID. Cross, plus the Cupra Raval and Skoda Epiq, all based on the MEB+ platform.
While those in the US won’t see the entry-level ID. Polo, Volkswagen is set to launch the ID. Tiguan in early 2027 as a replacement for the ID.4.

articles.title: Tesla cuts FSD’s speed margin from 50% to 10% over the limit in Europe
articles.summary: Tesla’s driver-assistance system in Europe can no longer be set to drive 50% over the speed limit. The Netherlands’ RDW, which approved the system in April, confirmed today that it signed off on an update capping the speed margin at 10% and officially renaming “FSD Supervised” to Tesla Assisted Driving. The changes land weeks before EU member states could vote on approving the system across the bloc, and they match the conditions Germany set last month. more…
bodyEvidence: Tesla’s driver-assistance system in Europe can no longer be set to drive 50% over the speed limit. The Netherlands’ RDW, which approved the system in April, confirmed today that it signed off on an update capping the speed margin at 10% and officially renaming “FSD Supervised” to Tesla Assisted Driving.
The changes land weeks before EU member states could vote on approving the system across the bloc, and they match the conditions Germany set last month.

The RDW’s notice is the clearest official confirmation of how the system was configured when the Dutch regulator approved FSD Supervised on April 10 . The “speed margin,” which lets the system deviate from the detected limit for “safety and traffic flow,” could go up to +50%. On a 100 km/h highway, that’s 150 km/h. In a 30 km/h city zone, it’s 45 km/h.
Now the margin tops out at +10%. It also resets to 0% every time the car starts, and the RDW says other speed-related functions are now disabled by default. It didn’t say which ones.
The new name shows up on the in-car display, in the owner’s manual, and in other driver information on HW4 vehicles. Tesla pushes all of it over the air.

The RDW describes the update as “several minor changes” that Tesla asked it to assess. The regulator says it checked the implementation, found no adverse or unintended effects, and folded the changes into the existing type approval without amending or extending it. It also stresses that the rename doesn’t change what the system does. It’s still driver assistance, and the driver is still responsible.

The RDW notified the nine member states that recognize its approval: Belgium, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia, and Slovenia. That’s 10 countries counting the Netherlands, up from eight at the start of October.

The EU-wide decision still sits with the Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV). The RDW says those talks are confidential and won’t comment on them. As we reported, the EU pushed the vote to December at the earliest , and passing it takes a qualified majority: 15 of 27 member states representing at least 65% of the EU population.

Speed has been the biggest problem for Tesla’s file in Brussels. In June, Sweden asked the EU to reject FSD unless Tesla removed the ability to set speeds above the posted limit. In September, a Brussels pedestrian safety group found the system speeding in 55% of the 30 km/h segments it tested , in a country that had already approved it. France has cited urban speeding as one of its reasons for refusing to recognize the Dutch approval.

Then, on October 6, Germany’s Transport Ministry said it would back EU approval after Tesla agreed to drop the “Full Self-Driving” name, which the ministry called misleading, and to cap speed tolerance at 10%. Today’s RDW update delivers both.
But 10% isn’t what Sweden asked for. Sweden wanted no setting above the limit at all. Several European countries are known for enforcing speed limits strictly.
Good, but that’s only part of the problem. Tesla’s biggest issue with FSD right now is that it doesn’t properly detect the speed limits.

Doing 10% over the limit in North America is almost expected. However, in Europe you can get a speeding ticket for 5 kms over the limit by an automated camera/radar system. When I rent a car over there I drive the posted limit.
Being locked at 10% over the limit doesn’t mean much if you don’t know the actual limit.

The name change is needed globally and it is past due. “Tesla Assisted Driving” describes what the system does. Meanwhile, Tesla still sells the exact same kind of software in the US as “Full Self-Driving (Supervised)” for $99 a month. If it’s misleading in Berlin, it’s misleading in California.
Practically, this update gets Tesla Germany’s vote. The question for December is whether a 10% cap is enough for France, Italy, and Spain, or whether Sweden’s zero-tolerance line wins out.

articles.title: Apple now lets developers offer discounts when users move to cancel subscriptions
articles.summary: Apple today rolled out a new subscription retention tool for developers looking to reduce cancellations. Here are the details. more…
bodyEvidence: Apple today rolled out a new subscription retention tool for developers looking to reduce cancellations. Here are the details.

During WWDC earlier this year, Apple announced Retention Messaging, a new feature that lets developers display personalized messages and special offers to users as they attempt to cancel their subscriptions.

Now, as the company explained in a new post on its developer blog, the feature is available, allowing developers to configure messages that “appear in the cancellation flow and can include text, images, or a special offer.”
If this sounds familiar, that’s because this is not Apple’s first attempt to help developers reduce cancellations.
In 2024, Apple announced Win-Back Offers , which allowed developers to offer discounts to former subscribers in an effort to bring them back.

What’s different about the new Retention Messaging feature is that it allows developers to reach subscribers before they complete the cancellation process, rather than after they’ve already canceled their subscriptions or let them expire.
Here’s Apple on how developers can configure these messages:

In App Store Connect, you can configure retention messages for your auto-renewable subscriptions, including subscriber eligibility and the wait time between messages. With the Retention Messaging API, you can choose which message to show each subscriber based on their subscription details. API access is available by request.
Apple’s documentation notes that developers can create up to 10 retention messages per app, each associated with one or more subscriptions.
To learn more about retention messages, follow this link .

articles.title: Report: Apple and Samsung outperform rivals as smartphone chip shipments tumble 21%
articles.summary: According to Counterpoint Research, Apple and Samsung were the only major smartphone chip vendors to gain market share in Q3 2026, as global shipments declined 21% year-over-year. Here are the details. more…
bodyEvidence: According to Counterpoint Research, Apple and Samsung were the only major smartphone chip vendors to gain market share in Q3 2026, as global shipments declined 21% year-over-year. Here are the details.

At this point, most 9to5Mac readers are probably familiar with the challenges that smartphone vendors have been facing due to rising memory costs, and how Apple has managed to weather the impact better than many of its competitors.

Over the past few months, many reports have noted that while most smartphone vendors raised prices more than once throughout the year, Apple held off on increasing iPhone prices until September, with the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro series.
Those same reports have been showing the iPhone outperforming the broader market in smartphone, even as the industry experiences a sharp downturn.
That said, Counterpoint Research recently published a report (via MacMagazine ) examining how rising memory costs and slowing smartphone demand have affected the global smartphone chip market.
According to the report, Apple remained in third place among smartphone chip vendors in the third quarter, with its market share increasing from 17% in Q3 2025 to 21%.
MediaTek still led the global smartphone SoC market with a 28% share (down 6 percentage points year-over-year), followed by Qualcomm with 22% (down from 25%).
After Apple, UNISOC ranked fourth with 13% (down from 14%), while Samsung remained in fifth with an 8% share, up from 6% in Q3 2025. Other manufacturers went from a 4% share to 8%.
Overall, the market saw a 21% decline year-over-year, though the report didn’t disclose how many chips were shipped during the quarter.
Commenting on the numbers, Counterpoint Research Senior Analyst Shivani Parashar said:

“We saw three notable flagship chipset launches in September 2026, based on TSMC’s 2nm process node: Apple’s A20 series, MediaTek’s Dimensity 9600 Pro and Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 series. These launches are expected to boost premium smartphone SoC shipments in Q4 2026, although volumes are still likely to remain below Q4 2025 levels.”

Looking ahead, Counterpoint expects global smartphone chip shipments to decline 20% year-over-year in 2026, followed by another 3% to 4% drop in 2027. The research firm also expects memory prices to continue rising next year.

During its fiscal Q4 2026 earnings call, Apple described the current memory pricing situation as “unprecedented,” warning that further increases would continue to put pressure on its profit margins in the coming quarters.
